description: Describes the exact fields pulse.mbta.map_rows reads out of a /predictions JSON:API page (one page = one HTTP response's parsed JSON body, before pulse.mbta.fetch_predictions merges pages together). Enforced by pulse.contract.validate_page against a live payload page; a silent MBTA schema change should surface as a named poll_runs error, not as a rising skipped/null count with no explanation. Only resource_types actually read by map_rows are covered -- route/stop/trip/vehicle resources appear in `included` but map_rows only ever reads their relationship *id*, never their own attributes, so a schema change confined to those resource types can't silently corrupt a mapped row and isn't worth gating on here.

direction_id.semantics: Read directly onto the row's direction_id (NOT NULL in stop_events; a row failing this clause is dropped by pulse.poll._prefilter before insert, but a MISSING or wrong-typed direction_id attribute is a contract violation regardless -- it means the field itself changed shape).

arrival_time.semantics: predicted_arrival. Null at an origin/terminus stop (MBTA gives departure_time only there) -- expected and NOT a violation on its own. A prediction with both arrival_time and departure_time null is skipped by map_rows entirely (schedule_relationship=CANCELLED), also not a violation.

departure_time.semantics: Used only to decide whether a prediction carries any temporal signal at all (see arrival_time's semantics) -- never itself written to a stop_events column.

status.semantics: Read onto the row's status column, which is structurally 100% null in the M1/M2 data -- see docs/lineage.md's status-column note. Nullable here reflects that reality, not a gap in the contract.

route.semantics: route_id. A null relationship produces route_id=None, which pulse.poll._prefilter drops before insert (route_id is NOT NULL) -- not itself a contract violation, since MBTA is not known to ever send this null; the relationship key's presence is what's contractually required.

stop.semantics: stop_id. Same nullability posture as route.

trip.semantics: trip_id. Same nullability posture as route.

vehicle.semantics: vehicle_id. Observed null on real trips (e.g. no vehicle currently assigned) -- nullable is the expected steady state, not a degraded one.

schedule.semantics: Joined against `included` (type=schedule) by this id to populate scheduled_arrival. Null on ADDED trips (schedule_relationship=ADDED has no scheduled counterpart) -- expected, not a violation.

arrival_time.semantics: scheduled_arrival. Null at an origin/terminus stop (schedule carries departure_time only there) -- expected, not a violation.

service_date.semantics: Overrides map_rows' polled_at-derived fallback service_date when present. As fetched today (include=schedule,vehicle) this field has never been observed on a live payload -- its absence is normal, not a violation; the contract still names it so a future MBTA response that DOES include it (e.g. via include=schedule.service) is validated against the same type/nullability rule rather than silently accepted or silently rejected.
